previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic abdominal pain localized near her gastrostomy tube site, three days after a prior discharge. The pain was focal and tender on examination with a positive Carnett’s sign, suggesting abdominal wall musculature as the source. Imaging showed a nonobstructive bowel gas pattern and gaseous distention of the stomach, likely related to her complex surgical history, but no evidence of infection or free air. Tube feeds were held overnight and successfully restarted. Gabapentin was increased to 600 mg TID for improved pain control, and she continued erythromycin and rifaximin for bacterial overgrowth. Mild leukopenia improved without intervention. She met with a social worker, discussed coping strategies, and was discharged home with stable pain, a plan to follow up with her GI doctor, and instructions to repeat CBC in one week.

Brief Hospital Course:

conservatively with NPO, D5-IVF, pain control, continued PPI, 
sulcrafate, and histamine blocker. Since patient's pain seem to 
improve when tube feed is not running, we proceeded to hold her 
tube feed with pain control, while maintaining D5 to prevent 
hypoglycemia (a complication that she has experienced and is at 
risk for). Our ultimate plan at this point is to see if she can 
be maintain strictly from po intake. Over the next several days, 
we weaned her off D5 while monitoring her clinically. Her pain 
lessened and we were satisfied with the result. Her po intake 
was poor, based on calorie count, and therefore, marinol was 
started. This produced great results and patient was able to 
maintain 90% of her daily caloric needs (1400-1600kCal / 1800

asymptomatic. We also obtained ___ consult, and she was

outpatient setting. She also was arranged for a follow up with 
___ and their dietitian, as well as a follow up appointment 
with us in ___ weeks for re-evaluation of the tube. The plan is 
to pull the tube feed in several months.
